Integrate Kerberos authentication for HDFS sink using Spring Hadoop or custom Kerberos modules.
Leverage Spring Integration's JMX support for the JMX source module.
Use HBase client APIs for HBase sink implementation.
Implement File Roll sink using standard Java I/O or Spring's file writing utilities.
For the mass-ingest spike, evaluate Spring Data, Apache Camel, or custom database connectors as integration options.
assumptions: The project is already configured with Spring Boot and necessary dependencies (e.g., Spring Security, Spring Integration).
Kerberos infrastructure and LDAP servers are available for testing.
HBase and HDFS clusters are accessible for integration testing.
Existing codebase allows modular addition of new sink/source modules without major refactoring.
Spike for mass-ingest will focus on design documentation rather than full implementation.

activities.activity_description: Configure Spring Security to use file-based authentication and secure all endpoints at http://localhost:9393/.
Set up LDAP authentication provider and secure endpoints using LDAP credentials.
Define Admin and Viewer roles and enforce role-based access on secured endpoints.
Integrate Kerberos authentication for secure data writes to HDFS.
Research integration options, collaborate on design, and document design specifications for database ingestion.
Develop HBase sink module for random, real-time read/write access on Big Data.
Create File Roll sink to store events on the local file system.
Build JMX source module using Spring Integration to publish/subscribe to JMX notifications.
